critiques.concern: The deferred cut-transcript follow-up leans on a recurrence-gated revival ('a second attestation-replay failure counted in an appropriate tracker'), but the proposal records the n=1 v0.3.0 failure ONLY as a CHANGELOG erratum (Correction 1) and OQ3 defaults to opening no tracker. Cairn already ships the fix: the incident-trackers module is installed and is explicitly the rate-limit gate's 'parse target', with live trackers homing under dev/measurement/ — so the existing substrate (lesson #4) covers this.

numbered_critiques.concern: The erratum treats the redundancy and neutrality attestations as equally false, but they are not — a precision the proposal's own honesty-selling premise demands. Replay shows redundancy fail=6, and the attestation ("6 advisory R6 redundancy notes ... accepted for a private cut") CORRECTLY counted exactly 6 R6 findings and consciously accepted them as pre-existing debt. What is false is (a) the umbrella "quality_gate exit 0" and (b) the neutrality "all-info/justified" claim, which is materially false (99 fails, not zero). Framing both sub-gates as equally "does not replay / not advisory" overstates the redundancy problem.

numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: In the erratum, separate the two: the redundancy finding-count was accurate and honestly disclosed as accepted debt; the neutrality "all-info/justified" claim was materially false; and the "exit 0" umbrella is contradicted by the actual exit. This keeps the erratum itself precisely honest.

numbered_critiques.concern: C3 frames the first supersession as "review performing its kill function ... review killing a change on its own merits." But the record shows automated-review-committer was "Superseded in favor of" alternatives taken from the AUTHOR's own Response (an immediate practice under existing doctrine + a deferred follow-up), triggered by blocking finding R1 — that is gating AND improvement working together, the idea was reshaped, not rejected, and supersession is not rejection (the "0 rejected" number stays 0). The disposition was "superseded" (over-reached / superseded-by-a-plan), not "rejected"; calling it review's "kill function" reads as a hard rejection. In a correction whose whole thesis is honest record-keeping, this over-claim is the exact irony a skeptic (or the postdoc) will catch, undercutting C3's credibility.
numbered_critiques.grounding: dev/proposals/archive/2026-07-08-claude-automated-review-committer.md:8 ("Status: superseded"), :428-438 and :448-463 (Decision: "Superseded in favor of ... from the author Response"; "The fresh-context Internal panel gated it on its own text — three blocking findings"); R1 at :224-236; grep confirms it is the only superseded/rejected proposal in dev/proposals/.
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Reword the C3 addendum precisely: review's blocking finding (R1) led the author to supersede the proposal in favor of an existing-doctrine practice plus a recurrence-gated follow-up — the first recorded instance of the adversarial read materially blocking a change as written. Keep "gating CAN bite" as the point; drop "kill"/"killing"; use "superseded" precisely and state that the rejected count is still 0 and supersession is the distinct signal (not a hard rejection).

numbered_critiques.concern: Correction 2 invariant (iii) overstates enforcement for both C2 pointers, and check_cairn cannot force either to closeout. Facet A (profile.yml out of scope): invariant (iii) claims "The two repointed references resolve to a real file — enforced by the existing scripts/check_cairn.py claim-path/link check," but check_cairn scans only tracked Markdown (git ls-files '*.md'); dev/.cairn/profile.yml is a .yml file and is out of scope, so its repointed pointer is NOT machine-checked — only the PLANNING.md pointer (a .md, and only if backticked as a path token) is covered, so the "pointer leads nowhere class is closed by an existing mechanism, with no new tool" claim holds for one of the two pointers, not both. Facet B (deferred PLANNING repoint / inconsistent window): C1's CHANGELOG erratum + C2's profile.yml comment repoint at the implementing commit, but C2's PLANNING.md repoint "lands at a serialization point, e.g. goodnight or the plan archive," creating a window where profile.yml names the concrete file while PLANNING.md:34-40 still says the generic "dev/strategy/" directory — an inconsistent pointer pair that check_cairn will NOT red-flag (a directory ref resolves), so nothing forces closeout and the PLANNING repoint can silently be dropped.
numbered_critiques.grounding: scripts/check_cairn.py:47 ("Scanned set: the whole tracked Markdown tree") and :177-182 (tracked_markdown = git ls-files '*.md'); dev/.cairn/profile.yml is .yml; current PLANNING.md:34-40 uses generic "dev/strategy/" directory pointer; AGENTS.md shared-comm-file rule — verified this session.

Additionally, in the implementing plan make the PLANNING.md repoint a required, tracked closeout step tied to the plan-archive serialization (not left to "e.g. goodnight") so both pointers land consistent; and note that the implementing commit bundling CHANGELOG.md is NOT auto-carved (CHANGELOG is carved only in the goodnight-handoff commit), so it is approval-gated — the proposal's "under explicit instruction" should be stated as a hard requirement in the plan.

numbered_critiques.concern: Of the three corrections, C3 is the weakest fit for the stated Phase-A deadline ("before the postdoc installs") and the most interpretive. C1 (false attestation) and C2 (dangling pointer) are artifacts a skeptic/postdoc hits first when auditing the record (broad-look 135-152); C3 appends an argument to an internal 2026-05-20 metrics strategy note the postdoc is unlikely to audit at install time, and the proposal's own OQ2 asks whether C3 really belongs to the eventual PUBLIC case study. Bundling is defensible — all three are one low-risk record-text class, so this is NOT the forced-tool-split situation — but the Maintainer should have explicit per-correction accept latitude rather than an all-or-nothing unit.

Say so in the proposal so acceptance-as-a-unit isn't forced.

numbered_critiques.concern: Evidence-to-claim scope mismatch, plus an unmentioned third failure. The attestation's literal claim is "quality_gate exit 0" (the full gate), but the pinned reproduction replays only two --sub invocations. The OR-aggregation (report.failed = any fail) means the two sub-gate fails do entail full-gate exit 1, so the logic holds — but an erratum refuting a false "exit 0" is strongest showing full-gate exit 1 directly. Separately, running the full gate on the cut tree ALSO fails order-independence (fail=1, pytest exit 1), which is pytest/environment-sensitive and is not mentioned; a Maintainer running the literally-attested full command would hit an unexplained third failure.

numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Either add a full-gate "exit 1 vs attested exit 0" line to the erratum, or explicitly scope the refutation to the two deterministic filesystem-walk sub-gates and state why order-independence is excluded (pytest-based, environment-sensitive) so the Maintainer isn't surprised.

numbered_critiques.concern: The proposal header's cairn-internal-ref-allow rationale states a doctrine reference is "a citation to Cairn's published methodology, not an installed local file." That is the adopter-tree convention, but this IS the Cairn self-host repo where doctrine/ exists locally (ls doctrine/ returns dual-review.md, lifecycle.md, rationale.md, proposals.md) and check_cairn resolves those paths. So the suppression is a no-op here and its stated reason is contextually wrong; it also slightly reduces the safety net by exempting doctrine paths that would otherwise be checked. Harmless to correctness (all cited doctrine resolves and is accurate, verified this session), but a blemish in a proposal about record accuracy.

numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Either drop the doctrine-path ref-allow (the paths resolve in this repo, so the checker passes without it) or reword its rationale to reflect the self-host context rather than the adopter-tree citation convention.

(3) Sibling review-record-integrity R12:385-391, R5:322, plan-review:406-416. (4) Superseded automated-review-committer Decision:428-438/:448-463, bundling-R1:224-236, deferral-model:456-463; archive enumeration confirms exactly one superseded proposal (first-supersession claim holds; grep confirms 0 rejected). NEGATIVE SPACE no lens could exercise: the CONTENT of the yet-unwritten adoption record (C2) and metrics addendum — they do not exist yet, so their honesty/completeness/over-reach (does profile.yml's six-axis + three-module rationale fully recover the 2026-05-14 framework note?) is a review-of-artifact catchable only at plan/implementation/note-read time, and it is the exact class the showcase-arc sin embodied; OQ1's resolution (a Maintainer judgment on link-maintenance into the closed CHANGELOG entry); the root cause of the order-independence pytest failure on the cut tree (environment vs. cut-tree defect — full suite not run); whether the sibling actually carries a post-archive top-of-file pointer (OQ1's precedent, not load-bearing since default is no); check_cairn/claim_check over the nonexistent new artifacts; and the Maintainer's actual 2026-06-12 deliberation state (unrecoverable by construction — which is the proposal's own point).
consolidated.second_round_recommendation: Yes — all three lenses independently recommend an External (cross-type) read before the Decision, concurring with the proposal's own plan-review request and the sibling review-record-integrity precedent, and this consolidated panel concurs. The doctrine/gate mechanics themselves are sound and do not need a second Internal pass; the Internal floor is met by this pass, and the record-of-fact corrections plus the enforcement-invariant fix are near-mechanical once R1-R5 land. What an External, different-agent-type reviewer is best placed to stress-test: (a) whether the deferred follow-up's recurrence path must be armed now via the existing incident-trackers substrate or the revival condition reworded (R1); (b) the honesty framing of the erratum — \"hand-written, not fabrication,\" the reconstruction/over-reach guard, and the redundancy-vs-neutrality precision (R3, R4); (c) whether Correction 2's reconstructed adoption note over-reaches its \"only what profile.yml + the 2026-05-14 framework note support\" boundary — unverifiable until written; and (d) OQ1 (may a link-maintenance pointer go into the closed 0.3.0 CHANGELOG entry, given proposals.md:132's \"written once\" vs :136-140's link-maintenance exemption). These are judgment calls a same-type reviewer sharing the author's priors is likelier to wave through (citation-precision items like R2 are themselves doctrine-recall slips a cross-type read catches better). External should gate the Decision, not the plan-open.
